title: User-controlled scheduler hint string used as getattr attribute name on HostState object
detail: In _parse_string (line 93-112), strings from scheduler hint queries that start with '$' are interpreted as attribute paths into the HostState object. The first path segment is passed directly to getattr(host_state, path[0], None) (line 105) where path[0] is user-controlled input from spec_obj.get_scheduler_hint('query') (line 135), parsed via jsonutils.loads(). An API caller can supply arbitrary attribute names (e.g. '$__dict__', '$_sa_instance_state') to probe HostState's internal Python attributes beyond what the API normally returns. While there is no code execution risk (no eval), this reflects externally-controlled input into Python object reflection. Impact depends on what HostState exposes — cross-file analysis needed to enumerate sensitive fields.
